Page 1's St. Brendan Confession block explicitly prints Saturday 3:15-3:50 PM '(Wilson)', so high moving that Confession from Newfane to our-lady-of-the-rosary-wilson is also supported. bulletins.verdict: Page 6's Mayville flyer specifies Wednesdays May 13-October 28: '3-4pm Holy Hour, Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament ... Confession, Benediction', then '4-5pm Novena to Our Mother of Perpetual Help, Holy Mass'. High correctly replaces low's 4-5 PM Adoration with 3-4 PM weekly Adoration with Benediction and adds the 4 PM weekly Mass, preserving the exact May 13-October 28 season. The flyer expressly invites people to Fr. Romey's personal daily Mass, so it is not a closed/private Mass excluded by policy. Removing low's 4-5 PM Confession is supported: Confession is part of the earlier Holy Hour and lacks its own definite component start/end, so the larger event's hours must not be copied. However, high changes church_list_needs_review from false to true, a real full-output difference omitted by comparison.metadata_differences. The flyer explicitly places the chapel/Holy Hour at St. Mary of Lourdes R.C. Church, Mayville, and page 2 maps Mayville to 22 East Chautauqua Street, the known st-mary-mayville venue. No separately located unlisted worship venue is established on the reviewed eight pages; the chapel is at a listed church, so the true review flag is unsupported. Mixed raster schedule gains and metadata harm prevent a net-safe advantage. September 27, 2026 published_date and wrong_bulletin=false are supported. Page 7's New Year's notes are equivalent special-occasion wording, not timing corrections.

bulletins.mechanism: Native-text perpetual-Adoration interval encoding ambiguity, not a recovered time or venue.
bulletins.verdict: Page 2 explicitly prints 'Immaculate Conception-Adoration 24/7 (call office for code to Chapel)'. Both outputs retain all seven weekly Immaculate Conception, Wellsville entries with midnight starts and a 24/7 chapel note; low ends each at 11:59 PM, while high leaves each end null. The source supports continuous availability, not a literal nightly 11:59 PM closure, but neither prints a midnight start or a finite end, and current schedule_policy.py specifies no dedicated representation for perpetual Adoration. A null end plus 24/7 note and a whole-day interval plus the same note are competing encodings of the same printed schedule. The PDF alone does not establish a definite net improvement or harm from this representational change; individual gain/harm remain unknown rather than forced negative. This is not a missing raster phrase. September 27, 2026 issue date and unchanged false bulletin/church-review flags are supported; calling for an access code does not mean Adoration is merely by appointment.
